name: 49371-longprefill-7b-1gpu
hardware: 1x NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3, one GPU of an a3 node (sm90).
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1. One card, one in-process engine.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), 256 streams, warmup 512 requests, no cooldown, bounded at 1280 requests with a 900 s safety cap, client seed 49371. Warmup exceeds the stream count deliberately: guidellm retains requests still in flight at the boundary, so the discard is about `warmup - streams` and the measured population must be read off `request_latency.successful.count`.
workload: synthetic_text, single turn, no prefix_buckets, `request_format: plain` so the declared count is the wire count and no chat preamble is shared between requests. Fixed by construction: every request is exactly 1536 prompt tokens and exactly 4 output tokens (min=max on both), greedy at temperature 0.0, with `ignore_eos` set by the backend under `max_tokens`. Sampled text only approximates reuse-free prompts, so read the prefix cache hit rate off the run: a materially non-zero rate is a partially cached workload and not this setup.
purpose: A document classification service on one GPU, labeling long unique passages in a few tokens for 256 concurrent users.
launch:
# Engine: commit 1ef1c7ebba7f96d9835ade1fbd3658397e0b9be6 (`git describe --tags` =
# v0.23.1rc0-1040-g1ef1c7ebba7f9 -- a commit, not a release). Built in-process: no HTTP server.
model: ibm-granite/granite-4.0-h-tiny
tensor-parallel-size: 1
max-model-len: 2048
enable-prefix-caching: true
# Confirm the startup log resolves this to `all`, and stop if it says `align`: the mode is only
# reachable for a model class that declares support, and the engine's own config check can override
# a pinned value without failing.
mamba-cache-mode: all
seed: 0
dtype: bfloat16
